title: Fallback Anchoring and Customer Scripts
summary: Practical framing and ready-to-use scripts for customer-facing teams to anchor expectations during degradations, explain multi-region and model fallbacks, and preserve trust while minimizing churn.
priority_actions: Adopt the three-tier transparency ladder (acknowledge, timeframe, remediation)
Train CS and AE on the four canned scripts below
Add in-product banner templates to Console with a staged disclosure model
Coordinate follow-up remediation notes with SRE and Product within 72 hours
body:
Purpose
This brief provides short, field-ready language and a decision matrix for when and how to communicate with customers during partial capacity events, model-quality regressions, and region-level disruptions. The goal is to preserve trust by: 1) being proactive, 2) avoiding over-commitment, and 3) offering clear remediation paths and compensatory options.

Context & principles
- Customers value predictability more than perfect availability. Clear, repeatable fallbacks are a major trust signal.
- Avoid technical jargon for product and account teams; focus on user impact and mitigation.
- Use a consistent cadence: acknowledge -> scope -> impact -> action -> timeline -> follow-up.
- Anchor expectations using concrete trade-offs (e.g., slight latency increase vs sustained cost savings, or temporary model downgrades for deterministic availability).

Common scenarios and recommended posture
1) Partial capacity (some requests delayed or returned with queued responses)
  - Quick posture: "We’re experiencing elevated load on the inference cluster in region X. Some requests may see increased latency. We’ve enabled higher-capacity routing and temporary burst lanes to reduce queue times."
  - Offer: auto-fallback to a compatible model variant with a stated performance delta ("~2–5% quality variance on average").
  - When to escalate: multiple customers in the same org report >3x tail latency or error rates exceed SLA thresholds.

2) Model-quality regression (internal rollout caused unexpected output drift)
  - Quick posture: "We’ve identified a model rollout that is generating inconsistent outputs for a small subset of prompts. We rolled the previous verified variant back for affected customers while we investigate."
  - Offer: immediate rollout rollback + selective canary for affected routes + postmortem and prompt-set examples delivered within 48 hours.

3) Region-level outage or degraded networking between regions
  - Quick posture: "Region Y is experiencing networking degradation which may affect throughput. We’re routing traffic to nearby regions and applying our cross-region fallbacks. You may see a small change in latency/throughput while we stabilize."
  - Offer: prioritized routing for committed capacity customers; optional temporary read-only or degraded feature modes for sensitive workflows.

Audience-specific canned scripts
- Sales (prospecting / renewal conversations):
  "We design inference to be predictable: when capacity is constrained, Redwood automatically routes to verified model variants and nearby regions so your product stays online. For enterprise plans we provide prioritized routing and transparent incident reports—customers choose how aggressive the fallback should be."

- Customer Success (live incident first contact):
  "Hi NAME — quick update: we saw elevated errors affecting your project between 14:12–14:34 UTC. We routed requests to an alternative model variant to keep traffic flowing; this may slightly change some outputs. We’ve opened an investigation and will share an action plan and timeline in the next 2 business hours. If you’d like, we can roll you back to your previous pinned model while we complete the investigation."

- Solutions Engineering (technical briefing w/ customer engineering):
  "Root cause: autoscaler contention + model kernel mismatch for p99 sequence lengths. Immediate mitigation: route to variant V-compact (quantized) and enable prefix cache for warm traffic. Impact: p99 latency reduced from 2.1s to 620ms; expected quality delta: measurable for few edge prompts — we’ll provide prompt-mapping and help tune your prompt set."

- Public/status/product banner (short in-app notice):
  "We’re currently operating on reduced capacity in REGION. You may experience increased latency; requests are being routed to alternate regions/models to maintain availability. ETA for stabilization: 1–3 hours. [Learn more]"

Escalation ladder and expected handoffs
- Level 1 (CS/AE): acknowledge and set expectations; provide canned script; open ticket with SRE and SE.
- Level 2 (SRE/Platform): implement routing and capacity mitigations; provide timeline and technical log snippets.
- Level 3 (Product/Applied ML): rollback or patch model variant if regression; run quick regression tests on canonical prompt set.
- Post-incident (GTM + Product): joint postmortem and customer-facing summary + credits/compensations if SLA violated.

Competitive positioning shorthand (how to talk vs competitors)
- Against: managed single-region providers: emphasize our cross-region fallbacks and prioritized routing for Dedicated customers. Message: "Unlike single-region endpoints that drop traffic or degrade silently, Redwood routes to verified model fallbacks and provides priority lanes so your SLAs remain intact."
- Against: turnkey, low-cost providers that lack observability: emphasize our traceability and rollback controls. Message: "You can see token-level latency and cost impact, and revert or pin model versions without changing your integration."
- Against: DIY self-hosted runtimes: emphasize the unified API and production controls (canary, A/B, automated fallbacks) that remove operational burden.

Measurable comms goals for incidents
- First customer-facing contact <= 15 minutes for P1/P2 customers.
- Follow-up remediation plan within 2 hours.
- Post-incident customer summary delivered within 72 hours.
- CS satisfaction (post-incident NPS) target >= baseline - 2 points.

Examples: short incident narratives (ready to paste into emails)
- Minimal: "We experienced an issue that temporarily affected response times for requests routed through us in REGION. We routed traffic to an alternate region and a verified model variant; the service is now stable. We’ll send a full summary shortly."
- Detailed (for enterprise contacts): "Timeline: 12:03 UTC — high error rate detected; 12:08 — automated failover to V-compact model; 12:12 — cross-region reroute activated; 12:35 — traffic normalized. Impact: 4 customers had requests with elevated latency; no data loss. Remediation: roll back of rollout, kernel patch applied. Next steps: 72-hour postmortem + tailored eval of your prompt set."

Empathy-first language dos and don'ts
- Do: name the impact on customer workflows (e.g., "blocking exports" or "batches delayed").
- Do: provide specific next steps and time-bound promises.
- Don't: overpromise exact ETA for complex cross-region failures; instead provide ranges and commit to updates.
- Don't: bury fallback details in technical notes — surface them up front for non-technical stakeholders.

Appendix: fallback options catalog (short)
- Compatible model variant (quantized or smaller): fastest recovery, small quality delta.
- Cross-region routing: robust for region outages, added latency risk.
- Read-only/degraded feature mode: preserves core workflows at the cost of reduced capabilities.
- Prioritized routing (Dedicated customers): preserves throughput for committed capacity, requires entitlement.

Next steps for GTM adoption
1) Run two roleplay sessions with CS/AEs using the three scenarios above.
2) Publish in-product banner templates and link to this doc from Console incident playbook.
3) Coordinate a short one-pager for Solutions Engineering describing exact API knobs (pin, fallback policy, prioritized routing) and include sample curl snippets.

Owner notes and open questions
- Q: Do we want a standard credit policy for short outages vs degradations? Recommend: tiered credit table aligned to SLA classes.
- Q: Which customer-facing metrics should be included in the 72-hour postmortem? Recommend: affected requests count, p95/p99 delta, models involved, and compensatory action taken.

This document is intentionally pragmatic — ready-to-copy language for the field and a decision matrix to keep disclosures consistent while protecting product reputation.
